text:
Evan Lee: hey team, accepted the GitHub invite but it attached to my personal account (evanlee.dev) instead of my work one (evan@redwood.com). When I try to access private repos I get a 'request access' button. :confused:

Rina Gupta: welcome Evan! If you accepted with the wrong GitHub account we can either remap or resend. Do you want us to revoke the old invite and send to evan@redwood.com?

Evan Lee: yes please resend to the work email. I don't want to add the work email to my personal account.

DevOps Bot: Note: org enforces SSO + 2FA. Reissuing to a work email will prompt SSO and then team mapping.

people-ops: doing the reissue now. Evan, watch for invite to evan@redwood.com — accept and complete SSO.

Evan Lee: got the new invite, clicked accept, redirected to SSO page and allowed access. It shows I'm a member but I still can't push to repos (403) and `git clone` works though.

Rina Gupta: 403 on push usually credential mismatch. Are you using HTTPS or SSH for remotes? `git remote -v` will show.

Evan Lee: HTTPS: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime.git. When I push it immediately fails with 403 and my credential helper is offering my personal account.

Rina Gupta: try clearing stored creds for github.com (OS credential manager) and then push so it prompts and you can authenticate with the work account. Or use `gh auth login --web` to ensure the CLI ties creds to your work account.

Evan Lee: cleared Windows credential manager entries and ran `gh auth login --web` selecting my evan@redwood.com account. After that `git push` still failed once but then prompted and succeeded.

people-ops: quick follow-up: some folks have multiple SSH keys or agents offering a personal key first which causes permission denied errors. If you switch to SSH add your work key in GitHub Settings -> SSH and GPG keys.

Evan Lee: I switched one repo to SSH and had to remove the old key from the agent. Steps I used: 
```
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "evan@redwood.com"
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
```
Added the pubkey to GitHub and updated origin to git@github.com:redwood-inference/serving-runtime.git — pushes are working now.

Rina Gupta: Great. I'm adding you to teams: runtime and dev-platform which grant write access to serving-runtime and related repos. @people-ops please confirm team add.

people-ops: Evan added to runtime, dev-platform. You should see model-zoo, serving-runtime, and infra-deploy in your repo list. If anything still shows 'Request access' try refreshing the GitHub org page or sign out/in.

Evan Lee: I can see everything now. Quick question though: my VS Code auth kept defaulting to my personal GH account in the extension. Any tips to switch it?

Rina Gupta: In VS Code GitHub extension sign out and sign back in via the work account. Also check ~/.gitconfig user.email for the repo (not strictly auth but helpful for commits): `git config user.email` and set per-repo with `git config user.email "evan@redwood.com"` if needed.

Evan Lee: All set, thanks for the fast turnaround! One last note: when people accept invites and run into this, maybe include a short checklist in the invite DM about SSO, clearing creds, and SSH key steps. Would have saved me a round trip.

people-ops: great suggestion, Evan. We'll add a short checklist to the onboarding message flow. Welcome to Redwood! :tada:
